% ===========================================================================
%  I.1  THE MOMENT FUNCTION, THE JACOBIAN, THE VARIANCE
% ===========================================================================

\begin{definition}[The debiased moment function, and the two matrices]\label{def:moment}
For a nuisance triple $\zeta=(\varphi,L,\varrho)$ with $\varphi\in\mathcal V$, $L:\IR\times\IR^{p}\to\IR^{p}$
Borel and $\varrho:\IR^{p}\to[0,1]$ Borel, write $\widetilde W(\varrho):=W-\varrho(\Delta Z)$ and define the
$\IR^{p}$-valued \emph{debiased moment function}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:psidef}
\psi(\theta,\zeta)\;:=\;\Delta Z\,\Delta U(\theta,\varphi)\;+\;\widetilde W(\varrho)\,
L\big(\Delta U(\theta,\varphi),\,\Delta Z\big),
\end{equation}
with $\Delta U(\theta,\varphi)$ as in \eqref{eq:trialres}. Write $\widetilde W:=\widetilde W(\varrho)$ at the
true propensity, $\zeta_\star:=(\vdagger,L_\star,\varrho)$ as in \cref{def:weight}, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:psistar}
\psi_\star\;:=\;\psi(\theta_\dagger,\zeta_\star)\;=\;\Delta Z\,\Delta U+\widetilde W\,L_\star(\Delta U,\Delta Z).
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:JSig}
J\;:=\;E\big[\Delta Z\,\Delta Z'\big]\;+\;E\big[\widetilde W\,\ell_\star(\Delta U,\Delta Z)\,\Delta Z'\big],
\qquad
\Sigma\;:=\;E\big[\psi_\star\psi_\star'\big] .
\end{equation}
% EXTRACTED FROM THE STATEMENT OF def:moment on 2026-08-03, under the house rule
% (.claude/references/theorem-environment-style.md) that a definition carries
% CONSTRUCTION ONLY.  Three justification blocks left; each is now a clause of
% rem:momentread, verbatim, at the end of Part I of this file.  NO \label MOVED:
% eq:psidef, eq:psistar and eq:JSig all stayed in the statement.
%   -- WHY THE SECOND SUMMAND CARRIES ell_star AND NOT L_star, why it is the zero
%      matrix under A1, and why the two-summand form is kept: rem:momentread(1).
%   -- THE "DIFFERENT MATRIX" CORRECTION RECORD, and the conditionality that
%      survives it:                                          rem:momentread(2).
%   -- THE TYPING NOTE, form against value, and its transfer to hat J:
%                                                            rem:momentread(3).
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A sentence asserting the opposite stood here through dispatch 12:
% "J is the matrix of A3 and it is not E[Delta Z Delta Z']".  The claim entered as
% a round-2 CORRECTION -- round 1 had routed identification of theta_dagger through
% A3, and the repair (M-3) routed it through A1b(iv) instead, on the ground that A3
% is "nonsingularity of a different matrix" and is itself conditional on A2.  The
% conditionality half of that ground is right and survives; the "different matrix"
% half is false, and it was asserted and never computed.  Its negation was already
% proved in this same file at lem:nusigma(v).
\end{definition}

\noindent\emph{Notes on \cref{def:moment}.} Why the second summand of \eqref{eq:JSig} carries
$\ell_\star$ and not $L_\star$ and is nevertheless the zero matrix, why $J$ is not ``a different matrix''
from $E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$, and how the typing of $E[\widetilde W\ell_\star\Delta Z']$ transfers to
$\hat J$ are \cref{rem:momentread}.

% The optional argument is BRACED because it contains a `]' inside math:
% \begin{lemma}[... $E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$] closes the optional argument at the
% FIRST unbraced `]', which is the one in E[...], leaving the `$' unmatched.
% Four LaTeX errors, no PDF.  An environment-balance count cannot see this --
% nothing is unbalanced; the argument is simply cut short.
\begin{lemma}[{The moment is valid, its variance is finite, its $\theta$-Jacobian is $-J$, and $J=E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$}]\label{lem:momzero}
The moment has mean zero at the truth, a finite second moment, and derivative $-J$ in $\theta$; the
finiteness is delivered by the \emph{level} clause of A$2'$ and not by its derivative clause; $J$ is
the second-moment matrix $E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$, so no rank condition beyond A1b(iv) is needed anywhere;
and, with one further clause of C$2'$, the variance is strictly positive definite, so \cref{thm:rootn}'s
studentised conclusion needs no positivity proviso.
Suppose A1, A1b(iv), A$2'$(i) --- \textbf{both} clauses (i.a) and (i.b) --- A$2'$(iii), B1(i), (ii),
(iv.a) hold. \emph{Clause \textup{(i.b)} is in the list and not an ``if in
addition'', for two reasons.} First, every bound below runs through \cref{cor:elldiff}, which
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft carried (i.b) only as an "if in addition".
is stated at an admissible representer \emph{in the sense of A2b} --- and A2b requires
$\Lambda^{(0)},\Lambda^{(1)}<\infty$ and continuous $u$-differentiability, that is (i.a) \textbf{and} (i.b).
Second, A$2'$(i)'s closing clause fixes $\ell_\star$ \emph{pointwise} ``from that version'' --- the version
satisfying both --- so \emph{$\ell_\star$ is not even pointwise well defined from \textup{(i.a)} alone}, and a
sup-norm statement about it is not well posed. \cref{thm:rootn}'s group (T-2) lists both clauses, so no
result downstream is affected. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $E\|\psi_\star\|<\infty$ and $E\big[\psi_\star\big]=0$;
\item[(ii)] $E\|\psi_\star\|^{2}<\infty$, so $\Sigma$ in \eqref{eq:JSig} is a well-defined finite positive
semidefinite matrix, with
\[
E\|\psi_\star\|^{2}\;\le\;2\,E\big\|\Delta Z\,\Delta U\big\|^{2}
+4\,E\big\|b_\star(\Delta Z)\big\|^{2}+4\,\big\|\ell_\star\big\|_\infty^{2}\,E\big[\Delta U^{2}\big] ;
\]
\item[(iii)] $\theta\mapsto E[\psi(\theta,\zeta_\star)]$ is twice differentiable on $\IR^{p}$ with
$\partial_\theta E[\psi(\theta,\zeta_\star)]\big|_{\theta=\theta_\dagger}=-J$, $\|J\|<\infty$, and second
derivative bounded in norm by $\|\partial_u\ell_\star\|_\infty E\|\Delta Z\|^{2}$ uniformly in $\theta$
--- the first derivative using $\Lambda^{(0)}_\star$ and the second using both budgets;
\item[(iv)] \emph{the debiasing summand of $J$ vanishes, and the $\theta$-map is exactly affine.} Under
A1's \emph{first} clause,
\[
E\big[\widetilde W\,\ell_\star(\Delta U,\Delta Z)\,\Delta Z'\big]\;=\;0,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
J\;=\;E\big[\Delta Z\,\Delta Z'\big] ;
\]
consequently $J$ is symmetric positive semidefinite, and $J$ is nonsingular by A1b(iv) alone. Moreover
$E\big[\widetilde W\,L_\star\big(\Delta U(\theta,\vdagger),\Delta Z\big)\big]=0$ at every
$\theta\in\IR^{p}$, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:psiaffine}
E\big[\psi(\theta,\zeta_\star)\big]\;=\;-\,E\big[\Delta Z\,\Delta Z'\big]\,\big(\theta-\theta_\dagger\big)
\qquad\text{for every }\theta\in\IR^{p} ,
\end{equation}
which is affine with nonsingular gradient: the \emph{population} moment has $\theta_\dagger$ as its unique
root on all of $\IR^{p}$, and its second derivative is the zero matrix;
\item[(v)] \emph{the variance is strictly positive definite, and no hypothesis beyond \textup{(ii)}'s list
plus C2$'$(i) is needed for it.} If in addition C2$'$(i) holds, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sigmapd}
\Sigma\;\succ\;0,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}\;\succ\;0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\vartheta'J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}\vartheta>0\ \text{ for every }\vartheta\ne0 .
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Clause \textup{(v)} converts a \textbf{proviso} of \cref{thm:rootn} into
a \textbf{consequence} of its hypotheses.} That theorem's studentised conclusion is stated for directions
$\vartheta$ with $\vartheta'J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}\vartheta>0$, which reads as a condition the user must
check; \eqref{eq:sigmapd} says it holds at every $\vartheta\ne0$ under hypotheses the theorem already
carries in (T-1) and (T-3), namely A1b(iv) and C2$'$(i). \emph{The two ingredients are exactly those and
nothing more.} By \eqref{eq:sigsplit} below, $\vartheta'\Sigma\vartheta\ge E[(\vartheta'\Delta Z)^{2}\Delta U^{2}]$,
both summands of $\Sigma$ being positive semidefinite; A1b(iv) makes $E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$ nonsingular, so
$P(\vartheta'\Delta Z\ne0)>0$ for every $\vartheta\ne0$; and C2$'$(i) gives $\Delta Y$ a conditional density
given $\mathcal F_{XZW}$, hence --- since $\Delta U=\Delta Y-\Delta\vdagger-\Delta Z'\theta_\dagger$ differs
from $\Delta Y$ by an $\mathcal F_{XZW}$-measurable shift --- gives $\Delta U$ one too, so
$P(\Delta U=0\mid\mathcal F_{XZW})=0$ almost surely and $P(\Delta U=0)=0$. On the positive-probability event
$\{\vartheta'\Delta Z\ne0\}$ the integrand is therefore almost surely strictly positive, and
$E[(\vartheta'\Delta Z)^{2}\Delta U^{2}]>0$; finiteness is A1b(iv)'s $E\|\Delta Z\Delta U\|^{2}<\infty$.
\emph{The second summand of \eqref{eq:sigsplit} is not used}, so no overlap condition enters: A4(i) is what
makes that summand bounded \emph{below}, and clause \textup{(v)} does not need it.
\emph{Two things clause \textup{(v)} does not say.} It says nothing about the \emph{size} of $\Sigma$, which
is where A4(i) does bind (as $\varrho$ approaches a boundary the second summand diverges); and it is a
statement at a fixed $P$, not a bound uniform over a class of laws --- $\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma)$ may be
arbitrarily small at nearby $P$, which is the same pointwise-versus-uniform boundary
\cref{rem:rootnscope}\textup{(6)} draws for the theorem itself.

\emph{Three readings of \textup{(iv)} must be blocked, and each of the three is a place a reader will
over-generalise it.}

\emph{\textup{(iv.1)} Clause \textup{(iii)}'s second-derivative envelope is a correct bound on the zero
matrix, hence carries no information.} It is marked here rather than struck, on this file's standing rule
that a proved clause is retired in place. \emph{$\|\partial_u\ell_\star\|_\infty$, and hence A$2'$(i.b)'s
budget $\Lambda^{(1)}_\star$, is \textbf{not} thereby freed}, for two independent reasons: it is consumed
by \cref{prp:sharpquad}'s inheritance in \cref{lem:biasexp}\textup{(2)}, and A$2'$(i.b) is in any case
required to \emph{license} \cref{cor:elldiff} at all --- which is what makes $\ell_\star$ pointwise well
defined and $\|\ell_\star\|_\infty$ finite, and hence what makes \eqref{eq:JSig} a matrix. Only the
attribution at \cref{rem:rootnhyp}\textup{(1)} changes.

\emph{\textup{(iv.2)} It is a statement about $J$ and not about $\hat J$.} A4(i) puts $\varrho$ inside
$[\varepsilon_\varrho,1-\varepsilon_\varrho]$, so \cref{def:crossfit}(a)'s truncation is free at the
population propensity and the population $\widetilde W$ is conditionally centred; but
$\widehat{\widetilde W}^{(-k)}=W-\hat\varrho^{(-k)}(\Delta Z)$ is \textbf{not} conditionally centred, at
any $n$, and the second summand of \eqref{eq:Jhat} does not vanish. \cref{lem:sandwich} Step~3 is where its
cost $\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}\|_\infty\|\mathsf r_k\|_{L^{2}(P)}$ is paid, and that step is unchanged.
\emph{Replacing $\hat J$ by $\IE_n[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$ would also be consistent for $J$; it is not
done}, because it would break the exact identity $\partial_\theta\bar\psi_n(\theta)=-\hat J(\theta)$ of
\cref{def:onestep} on which \cref{thm:rootn} Step~1's algebra rests.

\emph{\textup{(iv.3)} It does not propagate to the $\varphi$-direction, and the block would collapse if it
did.} $\Delta h$ is $\sigma(X_1,X_2)$-measurable and \textbf{not}
$\sigma(\Delta U,\Delta Z)$-measurable, so $E[\widetilde W\ell_\star\Delta h]$ is not zero --- indeed A2 is
precisely the assertion that it equals $-E[\Delta Z\Delta h]$ for every $h\in\mathcal V$
(\cref{prp:orthog}\textup{(i)} and \eqref{eq:orthphi}), and were it zero for every $h$ one would have
$\nu_{\Delta Z}\equiv0$, which fails at any design in which the instrument moves the regressor.
\emph{The boundary between the two sides is exactly the one \textup{(P4b)}'s warning and \textup{(P4c)}
were split to police}, and $q=E[\widetilde W\,\partial_u\ell_\star\mid X_1,X_2]$ sits on the non-vanishing
side of it.

\emph{\textup{(iv.4)} It does not touch $\Sigma$, and the one thing it \emph{does} say about $\Sigma$ is a
decomposition and not a vanishing.} The same tower step applied to the cross term of
$\Sigma=E[\psi_\star\psi_\star']$ --- legitimate because $\Delta Z\Delta U\,L_\star'$ is
$\sigma(\Delta U,\Delta Z)$-measurable and integrable by clause (ii) and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality
--- gives $E[\Delta Z\Delta U\,\widetilde WL_\star']=0$ and hence, exactly,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sigsplit}
\Sigma\;=\;E\big[\Delta Z\Delta Z'\,\Delta U^{2}\big]\;+\;E\big[\widetilde W^{2}\,L_\star L_\star'\big] .
\end{equation}
\emph{Both summands are positive semidefinite, and the second does not vanish --- for which one further
tag is needed and is \textbf{not} on this lemma's list}: under A4(i), $\widetilde W^{2}\ge
\varepsilon_\varrho^{2}$ surely, so $E[\widetilde W^{2}L_\star L_\star']\succeq
\varepsilon_\varrho^{2}E[L_\star L_\star']$, which is nonzero whenever $L_\star$ is. \emph{A4(i) is cited
for that sentence and for nothing else here}; \eqref{eq:sigsplit} itself, and every clause
\textup{(i)}--\textup{(iv)}, hold without it. \emph{The reading to
take from \eqref{eq:sigsplit} is the standard debiasing trade and not a defect}: with
$J=E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$, the sandwich $J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}$ is the variance the infeasible plug-in
\eqref{eq:prelimtheta} would have at a \emph{known} $\vdagger$, plus a positive semidefinite term; what the
debiasing weight buys is not variance but the removal of the first-order bias
$\langle\nu/\pi,h_k\rangle$ that \cref{lem:prelimtheta} Step~4$'$ shows the plug-in carries at exact order
$\|h_k\|$. \emph{Neyman orthogonality is untouched throughout}, being a statement about the three
\emph{nuisance} directions of \cref{prp:orthog} and not about $\partial_\theta$.
\emph{One simplification is available and is \textbf{not} taken into the displays}: since $J$ is
symmetric, $J^{-1\prime}=J^{-1}$, so \cref{thm:rootn}'s $J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}$ and
\eqref{eq:Sighat}'s $\hat V$ could drop a transpose. They do not, because $\hat J$ is \emph{not} symmetric
by \textup{(iv.2)}, and a variance estimator that dropped the transpose would not be symmetric either.
\emph{The transpose is carried in both places so that the population display and the sample display have
the same shape}, which is the convention \cref{lem:sandwich}\textup{(ii)} states the limit in.

\emph{A$2'$\textup{(ii)} is not among the hypotheses and is consumed nowhere in Part~I.} The variance object
is $E[\widetilde W^{2}\|L_\star\|^{2}]$, which clause (ii) bounds through A$2'$(iii) and
$\|\ell_\star\|_\infty$; A$2'$(ii) bounds $E[\widetilde W^{2}\|\ell_\star\|^{2}]$, a different quantity, and
that quantity is in any case \emph{implied by A$2'$\textup{(i)} in full together with B1(i), (ii), (iv.a)}:
\cref{cor:elldiff} gives $\|\ell_\star\|_\infty\le\|\varpi_u\|_\infty\Lambda^{(0)}_\star<\infty$ and
$|\widetilde W|\le1$ by (P1), so
$E[\widetilde W^{2}\|\ell_\star\|^{2}]\le\|\ell_\star\|_\infty^{2}<\infty$ with no further hypothesis.
\emph{The attribution matters}: the redundancy is \textbf{not} ``A$2'$(ii)
is implied by A$2'$(i.a)'', which is not a statement this file can make, since the only route to
$\|\ell_\star\|_\infty<\infty$ available here is \cref{cor:elldiff} and that corollary is stated at A2b.
\emph{The redundancy is real; its ground is A$2'$(i) in full plus the three B1 clauses.}
A$2'$(ii) is \textbf{retired in place} at A2$'$, on the
A3 precedent --- a proved clause is retired, its number kept so a stale citation lands
somewhere. \emph{The forward
Step-8 need is the only ground for retention that survives, and it is a forward obligation rather than a
present consumer}; it is recorded at the retirement note.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft recorded the redundancy as "A2'(ii) is implied by
% A2'(i.a)".  This is the referent slip A4's comment (d) recorded, seen from the
% other side; the retirement was acted on in dispatch 14, and A4's comment (d),
% whose retention ground was "the clause the second-order and bias terms consume",
% was rewritten, that ground being false in this file's own record.
\end{lemma}

% ===========================================================================
%  I.2  THE ESTIMATOR
% ===========================================================================

\begin{definition}[Cross-fitting, and the fixed anchor of the $\varphi$-step]\label{def:crossfit}
Fix $\mathsf F\ge2$, not depending on $n$, and a partition of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ into folds
$\mathcal I_1,\dots,\mathcal I_{\mathsf F}$ with $n_k:=|\mathcal I_k|$ and
$\lfloor n/\mathsf F\rfloor\le n_k\le\lceil n/\mathsf F\rceil$, chosen independently of the data. Write
$\mathcal I_{-k}:=\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\mathcal I_k$, $O_i$ for the $i$-th observation vector of A0, and
\[
\IE_n[\varsigma]:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^{n}\varsigma(O_i),
\qquad
\IE_{n,k}[\varsigma]:=\frac1{n_k}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_k}\varsigma(O_i) .
\]
\emph{At $\mathsf F=2$ this is Part~H's split, with $(\mathcal I_k,\mathcal I_{-k})=(\mathcal I_m,\mathcal I_a)$.}

\emph{Convention \textup{(P8)}, re-declared for Part~I --- and the parts of \textup{(P8)} do not have the
same standing.} \textup{(P8)}'s \emph{transfer rule} and
its two companions --- the $O_P$ companion and the $o_P$ companion --- are \cref{lem:pconv}(i)--(iii),
stated at a \emph{generic} $\sigma$-field, written $\mathcal G$ there and instantiated here, and they apply
with no extension.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  Through dispatch 16 this clause read that the generic sigma-field
% was "unnamed there", which was true of the comment block those statements then
% lived in and is not true of the compiled lemma.
\textup{(P8)}'s \emph{conditioning convention} --- ``every expectation and every $O_P$ is
conditional on the auxiliary fold'' --- was stated \textbf{for Part~H}, at $\sigma(\mathcal I_a)$, and is
therefore \textbf{re-declared} here rather than inherited: throughout Part~I it is read at
$\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})$, with $\mathcal I_k$ in place of $\mathcal I_m$. \emph{The licence is the same
either way, since the convention is a reading of a proof and not a hypothesis; the sentence is not, and this
definition is where the re-declaration lives.} \emph{That $\sigma$-field is written out at every site and is
given no symbol}: the
three natural candidates are all claimed --- $\mathcal G$ is \cref{lem:density}'s closed span,
$\mathcal E$ is the best-approximation error of \eqref{eq:jackson}, and $\mathcal F$ is the Fourier
transform of \eqref{eq:usobolev} --- and \cref{lem:balance} and \textup{(P8)} already write
$\sigma(\mathcal I_a)$ out, so the convention is inherited rather than invented.
Every conditional expectation and every conditional $O_P$ below is at that
$\sigma$-field, and A0 supplies the independence of $\mathcal I_k$ from $\mathcal I_{-k}$, which with
clause \textup{(c$'$)} below is what \textup{(P8)}'s \emph{freezing lemma} consumes.
\emph{Which clause of \textup{(P8)} each site uses is named at the site, and the answer for Part~I is
\textbf{never the transfer rule}.}
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  Through dispatch 13 this paragraph said otherwise.
Each conditional bound below is produced by conditional Markov or conditional Chebyshev, hence holds at
\emph{every} threshold with a $\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})$-measurable numerator, and is converted by the
\emph{$O_P$ companion} when the numerator is unconditionally $O_P(1)$ after division by the stated rate
(\cref{lem:prelimtheta} Step~4, \cref{lem:sandwich} Step~2) and by the \emph{$o_P$ companion} when it is
unconditionally $o_P(1)$ (\cref{lem:epterm} Step~6, \cref{lem:sandwich} Step~8). \emph{The transfer rule
needs the conditional probability to vanish at a \textbf{single} moving threshold, which neither
inequality delivers}; that is the observation \textup{(P8)} already recorded for the $o_P$ case, now
applied to the $O_P$ case. What supplies the tightness of the numerators is A4(iii), A5(ii), (iv) and
hypothesis (R-a) of \cref{thm:rootn}.

For each $k$ the nuisances are computed on $\mathcal I_{-k}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{Propensity.} $\hat\varrho^{(-k)}$ satisfies A4(iii) with $n$ replaced by $n_{-k}$ and is
truncated to $[\varepsilon_\varrho,1-\varepsilon_\varrho]$ as in \cref{def:hatT}, so that
$\widehat{\widetilde W}^{(-k)}:=W-\hat\varrho^{(-k)}(\Delta Z)$ satisfies
$\varepsilon_\varrho\le|\widehat{\widetilde W}^{(-k)}|\le1$ surely and
$\mathsf r_k:=\hat\varrho^{(-k)}-\varrho$ satisfies $\|\mathsf r_k\|_\infty\le1-2\varepsilon_\varrho<1$.
\item[(b)] \emph{Structural function.} $\hat\varphi^{(-k)}$ is the estimator of \cref{def:lfstep}, run on
$\mathcal I_{-k}$ \textbf{at a fixed anchor $\theta_\circ\in\IR^{p}$ chosen before the data are seen}, and
$h_k:=\hat\varphi^{(-k)}-\vdagger$. \emph{The anchor is what removes the circularity, and it is licensed and
not free.} By \cref{cor:opsol} and \cref{lem:shiftinv} the population solution set of \eqref{eq:opeq} in
$\varphi$ is $\mathcal V_{CI}$ at \emph{every} $\theta$, so under A1b(iii) the $\varphi$-step targets
$\vdagger$ at $\theta_\circ$ as well as at $\theta_\dagger$; \emph{what is not $\theta$-free is the
conditioning of the inverse problem}, so \cref{prp:phirate}'s hypotheses (P-a)--(P-g), \eqref{eq:muhalf} and
A7 in the form \eqref{eq:a7amend} are read \emph{at $\theta_\circ$}, and $a$, $\mu$, $\mathsf R_\ast$ and
$\hat\delta_n$ are $\theta_\circ$-specific. This is \cref{rem:R1}\textup{(iv)}, used and not extended.
\item[(c)] \emph{Debiasing weight.} $\hat L^{(-k)}$ is an admissible weight in the sense of
\cref{def:weight}(b), $\hat L^{(-k)}=L^{\,\hat b^{(-k)}}_{\hat\ell^{(-k)}}$, generated by an estimator
$\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ of $\ell_\star$ that is Borel, bounded, and continuous in $u$ at every $(u,z)$;
$D_k:=\hat L^{(-k)}-L_\star$. \emph{Those three properties of $\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ are the minimum
\cref{def:weight}(b) needs to be well posed} --- they are what make $\int_0^u\hat\ell^{(-k)}(v,z)dv$ exist
and make $\partial_u\hat L^{(-k)}=\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ hold at every point --- \emph{and they are stated here
rather than inherited}, so that this definition is well posed on its own terms; hypothesis (R-a) of
\cref{thm:rootn} strengthens continuity to continuous differentiability, which \emph{one} clause of this
definition uses and only one --- \textup{(c$'$.2)} needs it to make the inner supremum of the second
envelope, $\sup_u\|\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}(u,z)\|$, attained on a countable dense set and hence
measurable. \emph{So the sup-norm convention \eqref{eq:supnormconv} is \textbf{not} unconditional.}

\cref{lem:balance}'s sample-splitting convention --- the Part~F original --- states

$L^{2}(P_{\Delta U,\Delta Z})$ together with a fixed \emph{jointly measurable representative}, which is
strictly weaker than \eqref{eq:prodmeas} below and is all that site needs, it evaluating $\hat\ell$ at an

\item[(c$'$.1)] \emph{Measurability --- and it is two different statements, because three of the five are
only ever integrated and two are evaluated pointwise at arguments their container does not control.}

\emph{The three integrated nuisances, as random elements of $L^{2}$ at a fixed representative.} Each of
$\hat\varrho^{(-k)}$, $\hat b^{(-k)}$ and $\hat\varphi^{(-k)}$ is a
\textbf{$\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})$-measurable random element} of, respectively, $L^{2}(P_{\Delta Z})$,
$L^{2}(P_{\Delta Z})$ and $\mathcal V$ --- \emph{a measurable map from the sample space into the space, and
not a family of functions indexed by the sample point}. A random element of an $L^{2}$ space over a
separable metric space admits a jointly measurable representative --- measurable with respect to the
product of the sample $\sigma$-algebra with $\mathfrak B(\IR^{p})$ for the first two and with
$\mathfrak B(\mathcal X)$ for the third --- \emph{fix one for each, once, as A2c does for
$\ell^\Pi_\star$}.
\emph{For the third of the three this is a \textbf{discharged verification} and not a requirement, and the
difference is not cosmetic.} Clause \textup{(b)} pins $\hat\varphi^{(-k)}$ to \cref{def:lfstep}, whose

formula'', one Part earlier --- is unavailable: no formula is inspected when an index is chosen by a
discrepancy rule. \emph{What supplies it instead is the measurability paragraph of \cref{def:lfstep}}, which
builds the property from the deterministic cap \eqref{eq:cap}, the emptiness convention of

index of finitely many measurable events, the iterates are finite compositions of measurable maps, and the
stopped iterate is a finite indicator-weighted sum of them. \emph{The superscripts are not written out here},
because \cref{def:lfstep}'s index is a \emph{stage} index and this clause's is a \emph{fold} index, and the
two are one glyph apart. \emph{The other two remain requirements, as printed}, and $\hat b^{(-k)}$'s is read
off its formula on the $\hat\varrho$ model.
\emph{The sample $\sigma$-algebra is written out and given no symbol}, because
calligraphic $\mathcal F$ is A2c's Fourier transform and $\mathcal F_{XZW}$ never appears
without its subscript; the same convention applies to $\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})$
itself.

\emph{For these three the choice of representative is immaterial, and that is the test a container has to

and $f_{X_2}$. \emph{What transfers the null sets there is \textbf{domination}, and it has a tag}: C1(ii)

third object}. Either way any two representatives

$\varepsilon_\varrho\le|\widehat{\widetilde W}^{(-k)}|\le1$ holds \emph{surely}, as clause \textup{(a)}
says. The $L^{2}$ container is retained
for $\hat\varrho^{(-k)}$ only because A4(iii)'s \emph{rate} is an $L^{2}$ statement; it is not what any
pointwise bound rests on.

\emph{The two weight objects, for which the $L^{2}$ container is not merely unnecessary but wrong.} What is
required of $\hat\ell^{(-k)}$, in addition to clause \textup{(c)}, is that its \emph{own} pointwise
function --- the one \textup{(c)} already defines, at every realisation and every $(u,z)$ --- be product
measurable:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prodmeas}
(\omega,u,z)\;\longmapsto\;\hat\ell^{(-k)}(\omega)(u,z)
\quad\text{is}\quad
\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})\otimes\mathfrak B\big(\IR\times\IR^{p}\big)\text{-measurable} ,
\end{equation}
and $\hat L^{(-k)}=L^{\,\hat b^{(-k)}}_{\hat\ell^{(-k)}}$ then \emph{inherits} the same property from
\eqref{eq:weightdef}, together with the representative fixed above for $\hat b^{(-k)}$ --- \emph{so
\eqref{eq:prodmeas} is imposed on one object and not on two}. \emph{The inheritance is the
\textbf{measurability half} of Fubini--Tonelli and it is taken on positive and negative parts,
coordinatewise}: \eqref{eq:weightdef}'s integrand is $\IR^{p}$-valued and
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A dispatch-15 draft elided this to "by Tonelli's theorem applied to
% int_0^u hat-ell^{(-k)}(v,z) dv".
of arbitrary sign, and $\int_0^u=-\int_u^0$ when $u<0$. For each coordinate $j\le p$ and each sign part the
two maps
\[
(\omega,u,z)\;\longmapsto\;\int_\IR\un\{0\le v\le u\}\,\big(\hat\ell^{(-k)}_j\big)^{\pm}(\omega)(v,z)\,dv,
\qquad
(\omega,u,z)\;\longmapsto\;\int_\IR\un\{u\le v\le0\}\,\big(\hat\ell^{(-k)}_j\big)^{\pm}(\omega)(v,z)\,dv
\]
are product measurable by Tonelli's theorem, their integrands being non-negative and
$\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})\otimes\mathfrak B(\IR\times\IR\times\IR^{p})$-measurable by \eqref{eq:prodmeas};
all four are \emph{finite} at every point because clause \textup{(c)} makes $\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ bounded at
each realisation, so their signed combination is well defined and product measurable. \emph{This is the
device A2c\textup{(m.2)} already owns}, one Part earlier and on the other side of the
pairing, where the same positive-and-negative-part split carries Tonelli across a signed
$u$-integral. \emph{Under (R-a) the derivative inherits it too, and \textup{(c$'$.2)} needs that for its
second envelope}: $\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ exists at every point under (R-a) and is the pointwise limit
of the difference quotients of $\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ in $u$ taken along the reciprocals of the positive
integers --- \emph{the increment is written out and carries no letter}, on the same ground as
\eqref{eq:supnormconv}'s countable dense set; each such quotient is product measurable by
\eqref{eq:prodmeas}, and a pointwise limit of countably many product-measurable functions is product
measurable. \emph{A representative of an $L^{2}$ class supplies nothing of the kind}, having no derivative
in general.
\emph{No equivalence class is formed and no representative is chosen, so there is nothing
for a choice of representative to disturb, and clause \textup{(c)}'s continuity in $u$ is untouched.}
\emph{Why the $L^{2}$ reading fails here and not three lines above}: these two are evaluated at a

\emph{What is retained from the $L^{2}$ reading}, because several results use it, is membership:

above for $\hat\varphi^{(-k)}$, so both halves of this clause are load-bearing and neither covers the

holds, in either direction.} Not sufficient: the composite is product
measurable only once $f$ is itself jointly Borel in its two arguments, and at the sites where the

direction the proofs use}, and it is the one this clause is for: \eqref{eq:prodmeas} is what this

definition \emph{supplies}, and it is what the per-realisation ``Borel'' of clause \textup{(c)} does not. \emph{The file owns the device by which \eqref{eq:prodmeas} is verified, and it
is recorded rather than imposed}: \cref{lem:biasexp} Step~1 obtains joint measurability in

$\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})\otimes\mathfrak B(\IR^{p})$-measurable, since \textup{(c)} already makes

\item[(c$'$.2)] \emph{The sup-norms are essential suprema in $z$ and genuine suprema in $u$.} For the two
envelopes (R-a) prices,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:supnormconv}
\big\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}\big\|_\infty
\;:=\;\operatorname{ess\,sup}_{z}\ \Big\{\ \sup_{u\in\IR}\ \big\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}(u,z)\big\|\ \Big\} ,
\qquad\text{the essential supremum taken under }P_{\Delta Z},
\end{equation}
and likewise for $\|\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}\|_\infty$. \emph{Both halves of that reading are needed and
neither can be interchanged with the other.} The inner supremum is over an uncountable index but is
attained on a countable dense set, because \textup{(c)} makes $u\mapsto\hat\ell^{(-k)}(u,z)$ continuous at
every $z$ and (R-a) makes $u\mapsto\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}(u,z)$ continuous as well, so
$(\omega,z)\mapsto\sup_u\|\cdot\|$ is jointly measurable by \textup{(c$'$.1)}.

\emph{The \textbf{outer} essential supremum is measurable as well, and this does \textbf{not} follow from
joint measurability without an argument --- it is not a countable supremum.} \emph{The argument is the
tool of the previous
paragraph, once more.} At each fixed real level, the map
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A dispatch-15 draft of this clause carried the outer essential
% supremum on the word "likewise".
$\omega\mapsto P_{\Delta Z}\big\{z:\sup_u\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}(\omega)(u,z)\|>\text{that level}\big\}$ is
$\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})$-measurable by Tonelli's theorem applied to the non-negative jointly measurable
indicator; the levels at which that probability vanishes are exactly the levels \emph{at or above} the
essential supremum, since it vanishes at the essential supremum itself --- the exceptional set there being
the union of the countably many exceptional sets one reciprocal-of-an-integer above it --- and at no
smaller level, by the definition of the essential supremum as an infimum; and therefore, for every real
level, the event that the essential supremum does not exceed it is the intersection, over the
\emph{countably many rational levels strictly above it}, of the events that the probability vanishes ---
a countable intersection of measurable sets, the \emph{strict} inequality being what makes those
exceptional sets exhaust the one at the level itself.
Hence $\omega\mapsto\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}\|_\infty$, and likewise
$\omega\mapsto\|\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}\|_\infty$, is $\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})$-measurable as a map into
$[0,+\infty]$. \emph{The levels are written out and carry no letter}, on the same ground as the countable
dense set above (C12/C24/C78). \emph{This is load-bearing and not hygiene}: (R-a) prices both envelopes as
$O_P(1)$, which is a statement about the distribution of these two maps, and \textup{(P8)}'s $O_P$
companion requires its \emph{bounding numerator} to be measurable with respect to the conditioning
$\sigma$-field --- and at \cref{lem:sandwich} Step~2 that numerator is
$\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}\|^{2}_\infty E\|\Delta Z\|^{2}$, whose only random factor is the envelope. \emph{No
symbol of the companion's is imported into compiled text}; the numerator is named by what it is.

\emph{A genuine supremum over $z$, by contrast, would not be a measurable function of $\omega$}, since no
clause makes $z\mapsto\hat\ell^{(-k)}(u,z)$ continuous. \emph{And the essential supremum must be taken in $z$ and not
in $(u,z)$}, because every consumer of \eqref{eq:supnormconv} evaluates the envelope at a
\emph{shifted} first argument --- at $(\Delta U-\lambda\Delta h_k,\Delta Z)$ in \cref{lem:biasexp} Steps~1
and~4--5, at $(\Delta U_i(\theta,\hat\varphi^{(-k)}),\Delta Z_i)$ in \cref{lem:sandwich} Steps~2 and~9 ---
whose law need not be dominated by $P_{\Delta U,\Delta Z}$, while its \emph{second} argument is in every
case a draw of $\Delta Z$. \emph{The exceptional set is therefore $P$-null where the envelope is used}:
for each $i$, $\sup_u\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}(u,\Delta Z_i)\|\le\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}\|_\infty$ almost surely, and
the union over the finitely many $i\le n$ of the exceptional sets is still $P$-null, so the bound holds
simultaneously at all $n$ observations almost surely. \emph{For the deterministic $\ell_\star$ no
convention is needed and none is imposed}: A$2'$(i)'s closing clause defines $\ell_\star$ pointwise and
\cref{cor:elldiff} bounds it at \emph{every} $(u,z)$, so $\|\ell_\star\|_\infty$ is a genuine supremum and
the two readings agree.

$P(\max_{j\le\bar k}\|\hat\varphi^{(j)}-\vdagger\|_{H^{s}}\le\mathsf R)\to1$ --- where $\bar k$ is a
\emph{stage} index and not a fold index, the two being one glyph apart --- and it is a clause about an
\textbf{estimated} nuisance, so it is read at each fold complement exactly as the other three are: for each
$k\le\mathsf F$, A5(vi$'$)'s display is required of the $\varphi$-step run on $\mathcal I_{-k}$.
\emph{This costs nothing and is nonetheless not without consequence.} It costs nothing because $\mathsf F$
is fixed, so the fold reading is the intersection of $\mathsf F$ events each of probability tending to one;
it is not without consequence because the radius $\mathsf R$ must then serve all $\mathsf F$ fold
complements \emph{at one value}, $\mathsf R$ being a constant of \cref{def:srcball} and not a fold-indexed
object --- and $\mathsf R$ also appears in (P-c), (P-g), \eqref{eq:entropy} and, through
$\mathsf R_\ast$, in the schedule constants, so a fold-indexed radius is not available. (T-5) already reads
A5(vi$'$) at each fold \emph{operationally}, through ``\eqref{eq:phirate} holds on each
$\mathcal I_{-k}$''; what was missing is that this enumeration --- which declares itself the place where
the reading lives --- did not list it.
\end{enumerate}
Put $\hat\zeta^{(-k)}:=(\hat\varphi^{(-k)},\hat L^{(-k)},\hat\varrho^{(-k)})$ and, for $\theta\in\IR^{p}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:barpsi}
\bar\psi_n(\theta)\;:=\;\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{\mathsf F}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_k}\psi\big(\theta,\hat\zeta^{(-k)}\big)(O_i),
\qquad
\hat\psi^{(-k)}:=\psi\big(\theta_\dagger,\hat\zeta^{(-k)}\big).
\end{equation}
\emph{Since $\mathsf F$ is fixed, $n_k/n\to\mathsf F^{-1}$ and $n_k\asymp n$}; the constant $\mathsf F$ is
carried explicitly in every bound rather than absorbed, because \cref{prp:medianpart} quantifies over
partitions and a suppressed $\mathsf F$ would hide the one place a partition enters an order.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The preliminary and the one-step estimator]\label{def:onestep}
With the notation of \cref{def:crossfit} define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prelimtheta}
\hat\theta^{(0)}\;:=\;\Big(\IE_n\big[\Delta Z\Delta Z'\big]\Big)^{-1}
\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{\mathsf F}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_k}\Delta Z_i\big(\Delta Y_i-\Delta\hat\varphi^{(-k)}_i\big),
\end{equation}
on the event that $\IE_n[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$ is nonsingular, and $\hat\theta^{(0)}:=0$ otherwise. Define
the \emph{cross-fitted Jacobian}, for $\theta\in\IR^{p}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Jhat}
\hat J(\theta)\;:=\;\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{\mathsf F}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_k}
\Big[\Delta Z_i\Delta Z_i'+\widehat{\widetilde W}^{(-k)}_i\,
\hat\ell^{(-k)}\big(\Delta U_i(\theta,\hat\varphi^{(-k)}),\Delta Z_i\big)\,\Delta Z_i'\Big],
\end{equation}
so that $\partial_\theta\bar\psi_n(\theta)=-\hat J(\theta)$ identically, and put
$\hat J:=\hat J(\hat\theta^{(0)})$.
% WHY THE IDENTITY ABOVE USES ONE DERIVATIVE AND NO MORE, and why the second
% derivative is hypothesised at thm:rootn (R-a) and not here: rem:onestepread(1).
% The IDENTITY ITSELF STAYS -- only its proof moved.
The \emph{one-step estimator} is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:onestep}
\hat\theta\;:=\;\hat\theta^{(0)}\;+\;\hat J^{-1}\,\bar\psi_n\big(\hat\theta^{(0)}\big)
\end{equation}
on the event $\{\hat J\ \text{nonsingular}\}$, and $\hat\theta:=\hat\theta^{(0)}$ otherwise. The variance
estimator is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Sighat}
\hat\Sigma\;:=\;\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{\mathsf F}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_k}
\psi\big(\hat\theta,\hat\zeta^{(-k)}\big)(O_i)\;\psi\big(\hat\theta,\hat\zeta^{(-k)}\big)(O_i)' ,
\qquad
\hat V\;:=\;\hat J^{-1}\hat\Sigma\,\hat J^{-1\prime} ,
\end{equation}
the last \textbf{on the event $\{\hat J\ \text{nonsingular}\}$, with $\hat V:=0$ otherwise}.

\begin{remark}[How \cref{def:onestep}'s construction is read]\label{rem:onestepread}
\emph{Three clauses, each of which stood inside the definition. None of it is construction, and the
estimator \cref{def:onestep} defines is unchanged by its removal.}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] \emph{That identity uses \textbf{one} derivative and no more}:
$\partial_u\hat L^{(-k)}=\hat\ell^{(-k)}$, which \cref{def:weight}(b) supplies at every point under the three
properties \cref{def:crossfit}(c) requires of $\hat\ell^{(-k)}$, together with $\theta\mapsto\Delta U_i(\theta,\cdot)$
being affine by \eqref{eq:trialres} and the sum being finite. \emph{No second derivative is claimed here.}
$\partial_u^{2}\hat L^{(-k)}=\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ is used only at \cref{thm:rootn} Step~1, for Taylor's
theorem in $\theta$, and it is hypothesised \emph{there}, at (R-a) --- \emph{a definition should not carry a
differentiability claim that a theorem assumes}.
\item[(2)] \emph{The fallback is not optional.} $\hat\theta^{(0)}$ is given a value off $\{\IE_n[\Delta Z\Delta Z']\
\text{nonsingular}\}$ and $\hat\theta$ is given one off $\{\hat J\ \text{nonsingular}\}$;
$\hat V$ inverts the \emph{same} $\hat J$ and needs one too. That matters because
\cref{thm:rootn}'s \textbf{second} conclusion, $\hat V\xrightarrow{p}J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}$, and the
studentised statement that follows it are statements about $\hat V$ at every $n$, and a convergence in
probability is not well posed for a quantity that is undefined on an event of positive probability.
\emph{The choice of value is immaterial and the zero matrix is chosen because it is the one value that
needs no further object}: by \cref{lem:sandwich}\textup{(i)}, $P(\hat J\ \text{nonsingular})\to1$, so the
event on which the fallback is active has probability tending to zero and no conclusion of
\cref{lem:sandwich}\textup{(ii)} or of \cref{thm:rootn} changes. \emph{In a finite sample the fallback is
not innocuous and should not be reported as a variance estimate}: $\hat V=0$ makes the studentised
statistic undefined, which is the honest report on that event and is the reason the value is stated rather
than left to the reader.
\item[(3)] \emph{One step and not a root, and the ground is the \textbf{sample} criterion and not the
population one.} The realised map
$\theta\mapsto\bar\psi_n(\theta)$ is \emph{not} affine: by \eqref{eq:psidef} $\theta$ enters
$\hat L^{(-k)}$ through its first argument, and $\widehat{\widetilde W}^{(-k)}$ is not conditionally
centred, so $\bar\psi_n(\theta)=0$ need not have a unique root at any $n$. \emph{The ground is
\textbf{not} that no global rank condition is available}: by \cref{lem:momzero}\textup{(iv)} and
\eqref{eq:psiaffine} the
population moment $\theta\mapsto E[\psi(\theta,\zeta_\star)]$ is affine with gradient $-E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$,
so a global rank condition \emph{is} available, it is A1b(iv), and $\theta_\dagger$ is its unique root on
all of $\IR^{p}$ --- which says nothing about the sample criterion at estimated nuisances.
\emph{What the block supplies is a preliminary with a
rate} (\cref{lem:prelimtheta}), and a one-step from a preliminary with a rate is exactly the construction
that converts a rank condition on the population Jacobian into a limit distribution without solving
anything; the cross-fitted form is that of
\citet{chernozhukov2018dml}, and the two classical anchors for the one-step itself are
\citet[\S3.4]{newey1994h} and \citet[Ch.~5]{vandervaart1998}.
% CORRECTED 2026-08-03.  This sentence read that the two anchors "are NOT CITED
% HERE BECAUSE THEIR KEYS ARE ABSENT FROM THIS PROJECT'S BIBLIOGRAPHY", and
% flagged them for the librarian.  BOTH KEYS ARE PRESENT -- references.bib
% carries newey1994h and vandervaart1998, added in PASS 9 -- and the SPLIT
% MIRROR (results_s3_estimation.tex) has been citing them properly all along.
% So the undivided parent asserted something false that its own mirror got
% right, which is the sharpest instance to date of the parent/split divergence:
% not a formatting difference but a claim about the artifact that the artifact
% contradicts.  Retiring the parent in favour of the split is the standing
% recommendation; until that decision is taken, defects like this one have to be
% fixed twice or they persist in the file the corpus build validates.
\emph{The Jacobian is
evaluated at $\hat\theta^{(0)}$ and not at $\hat\theta$}, which is what makes \eqref{eq:onestep} a closed-form
estimator and what makes the algebra of \cref{thm:rootn} Step~1 exact rather than asymptotic.
\end{enumerate}
\end{remark}

%  I.3  THE FOUR LEMMAS

\begin{lemma}[L-14 with a rate: the plug-in preliminary]\label{lem:prelimtheta}
The preliminary inherits the first-stage rate, and it inherits it because $\theta_\dagger$ is identified by
restriction (B) alone.
Suppose A0, A1, A1b(iv), C1(ii) hold, adopt \cref{def:crossfit}, and suppose A5(ii)'s \textbf{first half,
read at each fold} --- the first display of \eqref{eq:foldrates}. \emph{The fold index is cited for the
reason \cref{def:crossfit}(d) gives}: A5(ii) prices one $h$, and \eqref{eq:prelimtheta} averages over
$\mathsf F$ of them. \emph{A5\textup{(ii)}'s second half $\delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/4})$ is \textbf{not} in this
list}; it is the hypothesis of clause \textup{(ii)} alone. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{the rate, on a list with no threshold in $n$;}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prelimthetarate}
\big\|\hat\theta^{(0)}-\theta_\dagger\big\|\;=\;O_P\big(n^{-1/2}\big)+O_P\big(\delta_n\big) ,
\end{equation}
and if in addition $\delta_n\to0$ then $\hat\theta^{(0)}\xrightarrow{p}\theta_\dagger$;
\item[(ii)] \emph{the threshold, which is the only clause A5\textup{(ii)}'s second half enters.} If in
addition $\delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/4})$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prelimthetathresh}
\big\|\hat\theta^{(0)}-\theta_\dagger\big\|\;=\;o_P\big(n^{-1/4}\big) .
\end{equation}
\emph{Both summands of \textup{(i)} are needed for this conclusion and neither is redundant to it}: the
first is $o(n^{-1/4})$ trivially and the second is A5\textup{(ii)}'s second half.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Why the split, and why it is \textbf{not} the \textup{(i)}/\textup{(i$'$)} device of
\cref{lem:sandwich}.} That device states \emph{one} conclusion on two lists; here the two clauses have
\emph{different} conclusions, so they are numbered and not primed. The split exists for
\cref{cor:ratefloor}, whose hypotheses deliberately omit A5(ii)'s second half --- doing without
\eqref{eq:frontier}, hence without that threshold, is what the corollary is \emph{for} --- and which
consumes this lemma twice: once for the fourth hypothesis of \cref{lem:sandwich}\textup{(i$'$)},
$\|\hat\theta^{(0)}-\theta_\dagger\|=o_P(1)$, and once for
$\|\Psi^{\theta}_n\|=O_P(\|\hat\theta^{(0)}-\theta_\dagger\|^{2})$. \emph{Clause \textup{(i)} supplies both
from its statement.}
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-11 draft stated only the conjunction of eq:prelimthetarate
% and eq:prelimthetathresh under a list containing A5(ii) in full, so cor:ratefloor
% had to be read against this lemma's PROOF -- the same defect
% lem:sandwich(i') was written to end, one lemma short of the end.
\emph{If in addition A5(i) and
A5(iii) hold}, then $\delta_n\gg n^{-1/2}$ --- because $\hat\delta_n=n^{-\alpha}$ with
$\alpha=r/(2r+d_Z)<\tfrac12$ and $\kappa=2\mu/(2\mu+1)<1$ give $\kappa\alpha<\tfrac12$ --- so the two
summands of \eqref{eq:prelimthetarate} collapse to $O_P(\delta_n)$. \emph{That simplification is cosmetic
and is used by neither clause}:
\cref{thm:rootn} Step~2 works at the uncollapsed rate \eqref{eq:prelimthetarate}, since
$\sqrt n(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n)^{2}\le2(n^{-1/2}+\sqrt n\,\delta_n^{2})$ and both summands vanish under A5(ii);
which is why A5(i) and A5(iii) are not among the hypotheses above.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft of this sentence said the collapse was "not on the
% path to thm:rootn" while Step 2 opened by using the collapsed form; Step 2 is
% restated at the uncollapsed rate and the two agree.
\emph{No condition on $\hat\ell$, on $\hat L$, on $\hat\varrho$, on $L_x$ or on A2 is used}: the preliminary
does not touch the debiased moment.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[L-6 and L-7 at the estimated nuisances: the exact bias decomposition]\label{lem:biasexp}
The conditional bias of the debiased moment at the estimated nuisances is the balancing pairing plus exactly
three remainders --- one quadratic in the structural error, two products of two estimation errors --- and no
Taylor expansion in the nuisances is taken.
Suppose A1, A1b(i), A1b(iv), A2, A$2'$(i), A$2'$(iii), N1, B1(i), (ii), (iv), C1(ii) and C2$'$(i) hold;
adopt \cref{def:crossfit}; and suppose hypothesis (R-a) of \cref{thm:rootn}, so that $\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ is
bounded and continuously differentiable in $u$ with
$\max_{k\le\mathsf F}\|\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}\|_\infty=O_P(1)$ --- \emph{an $O_P(1)$ envelope and
\textbf{not} a bound at every sample point}: \eqref{eq:biasb2}
carries the envelope on its \emph{right} and is read, as the displays below all are, on the event where
it is finite. Put $g_k:=\Delta Z+\widetilde W\,\hat\ell^{(-k)}(\Delta U,\Delta Z)$. Then, for every $k$, almost
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  This gloss read "||partial_u hat-ell^{(-k)}||_inf < infinity almost
% surely" through dispatch 20, which is neither what (R-a) states nor what
% eq:biasb2 needs.
surely
\begin{equation}\label{eq:biasdecomp}
E\big[\hat\psi^{(-k)}\,\big|\,\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})\big]
\;=\;-\big\langle\nu_{g_k}/\pi,\;h_k\big\rangle_{L^{2}(\pi)}
\;-\;\Psi^{(1)}_k\;+\;\Psi^{(2)}_k\;-\;\Psi^{(3)}_k ,
\end{equation}
where, all expectations being conditional on $\sigma(\mathcal I_{-k})$,
\[
\Psi^{(1)}_k:=E\Big[\widetilde W\,\Delta h_k\!\int_0^1\!\big\{\hat\ell^{(-k)}(\Delta U-\lambda\Delta h_k,\Delta Z)-\hat\ell^{(-k)}(\Delta U,\Delta Z)\big\}d\lambda\Big],
\]
\[
\Psi^{(2)}_k:=E\Big[\mathsf r_k(\Delta Z)\,\Delta h_k\!\int_0^1\!\hat\ell^{(-k)}(\Delta U-\lambda\Delta h_k,\Delta Z)\,d\lambda\Big],
\qquad
\Psi^{(3)}_k:=E\big[\mathsf r_k(\Delta Z)\,D_k(\Delta U,\Delta Z)\big] ,
\]
and
\begin{align}
\big|\big\langle\nu_{g_k}/\pi,h_k\big\rangle\big|
&\;\le\;2\,\bar c_\pi^{1/2}\,\big\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}-\ell_\star\big\|_{L^{2}(P)}\,\big\|h_k\big\|_{L^{2}(\pi)},
\label{eq:biasb1}\\
\big\|\Psi^{(1)}_k\big\|&\;\le\;2\,\bar c_\pi\,\big\|\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}\big\|_\infty\,\big\|h_k\big\|^{2}_{L^{2}(\pi)},
\label{eq:biasb2}\\
\big\|\Psi^{(2)}_k\big\|&\;\le\;2\,\bar c_\pi^{1/2}\,\big\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}\big\|_\infty\,\big\|\mathsf r_k\big\|_{L^{2}(P)}\,\big\|h_k\big\|_{L^{2}(\pi)},
\label{eq:biasb3}\\
\big\|\Psi^{(3)}_k\big\|&\;\le\;\big\|\mathsf r_k\big\|_{L^{2}(P)}\,\big\|D_k\big\|_{L^{2}(P)},
\qquad\text{and}\qquad \Psi^{(3)}_k=0\ \text{ if $D_k$ satisfies N1}',
\label{eq:biasb4}
\end{align}
where $\|\mathsf r_k\|_{L^{2}(P)}:=(E[\mathsf r_k(\Delta Z)^{2}])^{1/2}$.

\emph{The three remainders are written $\Psi^{(j)}_k$ and not $\mathcal R^{(j)}_k$, and the choice is
forced.} $\mathcal R(\cdot)$ is the \emph{range} of an operator throughout this file --- A2, \cref{lem:solset},
\cref{lem:srctransfer} --- and calligraphic $\mathcal C$, $\mathcal E$, $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal H$,
$\mathcal U$ are all claimed as well. $\Psi$ is the letter this project already binds to $E[\psi]$ along a
nuisance path (\cref{lem:secondord}), and these three objects \emph{are} components of $E[\psi]$ at the
estimated nuisances, so the letter is semantically right; $\Psi(\tau)$ always carries an argument and
$\Psi^{(j)}_k$ never does, which is the same separation device that keeps
$T(\cdot,\cdot)$ apart from $\mathcal T$. \emph{\Cref{prp:sharpquad}'s precedent --- ``the remainder carries
no symbol of its own'' --- is followed \textbf{where it can be, which is at two objects and not at three}}:
the Hessian envelope of \cref{thm:rootn} Step~1 and the event $\{\hat J\ \text{nonsingular}\}$ are written
out, while the $\theta$-remainder \textbf{does} carry a symbol, $\Psi^{\theta}_n$, because it is referred to
at six separate sites across two proofs and writing it out at each would be unreadable.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft of this sentence claimed the theta-remainder was
% written out; it is glossary slot C77 and the glossary row is the accurate one.

\emph{Three structural facts are visible in \eqref{eq:biasdecomp} and each is a claim of the paper.}
\textup{(1)} \emph{No second-order term in $L$ and none in $\varrho$ appears, exactly}, because $\psi$ is
bi-affine in $(L,\varrho)$ --- this is \cref{lem:secondord}\textup{(ii)} and it is used here as an
\emph{identity} rather than as a derivative statement, which is why \eqref{eq:biasdecomp} carries no Taylor
remainder in those two directions. \textup{(2)} \emph{The only square is $\Psi^{(1)}_k$}, and by
\cref{prp:sharpquad}\textup{(i)},\textup{(iii)} its order in $\|h_k\|_{L^{2}(\pi)}$ cannot be improved
uniformly over an $L^{2}(\pi)$-ball --- what is inherited from Part~G is the \emph{lower} bound on the
leading term, and \cref{rem:sharpscope}\textup{(1)} is what forbids reading it as a statement about the
realised $h_k$. \textup{(3)} \emph{$\Psi^{(3)}_k$ is the entire cost of N1$'$ failing at the estimated
direction}, which is obligation \textup{(O2)} of \cref{rem:obligations}, and \eqref{eq:biasb4} prices it.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[L-8: cross-fitting removes the empirical-process term]\label{lem:epterm}
Once the estimated moment is $L^{2}(P)$-consistent at a frozen nuisance, the centred empirical average of
the estimated moment minus the true one is $o_P(n^{-1/2})$ --- no entropy condition, no Donsker property,
and no stochastic equicontinuity at the estimated point. \emph{What is \textbf{not} claimed is that the
consistency is free}: \eqref{eq:psiL2} is established below from the rate and envelope conditions listed,
and the headline is a statement about what \eqref{eq:psiL2} \emph{buys} at scale $n^{-1/2}$, not about what
\eqref{eq:psiL2} costs.
Suppose A0, C1(ii), A4(iii) hold, adopt \cref{def:crossfit}, suppose hypotheses (R-a) and (R-b) of
\cref{thm:rootn}, and suppose A5(ii) and A5(vi) with $s>\tfrac12$ \textbf{read at each fold} --- the first
two displays of \eqref{eq:foldrates}. \emph{The fold index is cited rather than left implicit because A5(ii)
and A5(vi) are stated at a \textbf{single} $h=\hat\varphi-\vdagger$ while this lemma consumes them at
$\mathsf F$ distinct estimators}, one per fold complement; \cref{def:crossfit}(d) is where the reading is
declared and \cref{thm:rootn} Step~0 is where it is discharged.
\emph{A1b(iv) is \textbf{not} a hypothesis, on a ground of its own and
not on \cref{lem:opnoise}'s.} No step below cites it, and the two moments any step of this proof or of the
clause of \cref{def:crossfit}\textup{(c$'$.1)} it adopts could want from it --- $E\|\Delta Z\|^{2}$ at
Step~2 and $E[\Delta U^{2}]$ in that clause's derived $L^{2}$ membership of $\hat L^{(-k)}$ --- are
implied a fortiori by (R-b), which this list already carries and which asks for the \emph{fourth} moments
of both. What this lemma
does \textbf{not} use is A1b(iv)'s nonsingularity clause, which is \cref{lem:sandwich}'s. Then
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A1b(iv) stood on this line through dispatch 20; the deletion is a
% strict weakening and the two displays are unchanged.
\begin{equation}\label{eq:psiL2}
\max_{k\le\mathsf F}\big\|\hat\psi^{(-k)}-\psi_\star\big\|_{L^{2}(P)}\;=\;o_P(1),
\end{equation}
where the norm is taken at frozen $\hat\zeta^{(-k)}$, and consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eptermbound}
\sqrt n\,\sum_{k=1}^{\mathsf F}\frac{n_k}{n}\,
\Big(\IE_{n,k}-E\Big)\big[\hat\psi^{(-k)}-\psi_\star\big]\;=\;o_P(1).
\end{equation}
\emph{What is and is not conceded, stated because leg~3 of the Chen--Pouzo answer is a positioning
commitment.} \eqref{eq:eptermbound} is proved by conditional Chebyshev at a \emph{frozen} nuisance, so the
only input it requires is the $L^{2}(P)$ consistency \eqref{eq:psiL2}. \emph{This is a different
statement from \cref{lem:unifop}, and the difference is the point}: \cref{lem:unifop} concedes a uniform law
of large numbers with a rate over a slowly growing ball, at scale $\hat\delta_n\gg n^{-1/2}$, and that
concession is charged in the $\varphi$-step; the $\theta$-step concedes nothing at scale $n^{-1/2}$, which is
where a penalised sieve minimum-distance treatment of $\theta$ would need stochastic equicontinuity of the
$\sqrt n$-scaled empirical process at the estimated point.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[L-11: the sandwich, and no additional correction for the propensity]\label{lem:sandwich}
Both factors of the sandwich are consistent, and the sandwich is the \emph{whole} asymptotic variance: no
Neyman correction for the propensity appears in it.
Suppose the hypotheses of \cref{lem:epterm} \textbf{and of \cref{lem:momzero}}, together with A2,
(R-e) of \cref{thm:rootn}, and $\|\hat\theta^{(0)}-\theta_\dagger\|=o_P(1)$. \emph{\cref{lem:momzero}'s list
is inherited in full and not abbreviated}: Steps~3, 6, 6$'$ and~7 of the proof cite
\cref{lem:momzero}\textup{(ii)}--\textup{(iv)}, whose hypotheses run A1, A1b(iv), A$2'$(i), A$2'$(iii),
B1(i), (ii), (iv.a) --- the last three being the bridge \cref{cor:elldiff} needs to make
$\|\ell_\star\|_\infty$ finite, hence to make $J$ of \eqref{eq:JSig} a finite matrix. \emph{A3 is
\textbf{not} on this list}: Step~6 needs $J$
nonsingular, \cref{lem:momzero}\textup{(iv)} delivers $J=E[\Delta Z\Delta Z']$ and A1b(iv) delivers its
nonsingularity, and both are already on the inherited list. A3 is retired at A3. Then
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft listed A2'(i) and A2'(iii) and omitted A1 and the
% three B1 clauses, so it was short by exactly the cor:elldiff bridge.  A3 was on
% this list through dispatch 12; the deletion is a strict weakening with no change
% of conclusion.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\hat J(\theta_\dagger)\xrightarrow{p}J$ and $\hat J=\hat J(\hat\theta^{(0)})\xrightarrow{p}J$;
consequently $P(\hat J\ \text{nonsingular})\to1$ and $\hat J^{-1}\xrightarrow{p}J^{-1}$;
\item[(i$'$)] \emph{clause \textup{(i)} uses no rate in $n$, and holds on a strictly weaker list.} The
conclusions of \textup{(i)} hold under A0, A1, A1b(iv), C1(ii), A2, A$2'$(i), A$2'$(iii), B1(i), (ii),
(iv.a), A4(i)--(iii), \cref{def:crossfit}, (R-a), $\|\hat\theta^{(0)}-\theta_\dagger\|=o_P(1)$ and the three
consistency statements
\[
\max_{k\le\mathsf F}\big\|h_k\big\|_{L^{2}(\pi)}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\max_{k\le\mathsf F}\big\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}-\ell_\star\big\|_{L^{2}(P)}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\max_{k\le\mathsf F}\big\|\mathsf r_k\big\|_{L^{2}(P)}=o_P(1),
\]
the last of which A4(ii)--(iii) supply whenever $r_n\to0$. \emph{In particular A5(ii), A5(vi), (R-b) and
(R-e) are not used, and no product of two rates and no threshold in $n$ appears}; \eqref{eq:psiL2} is not
used either, clause \textup{(i)} being about $\hat J$ alone. This is the clause \cref{cor:ratefloor} invokes,
and it is stated because that corollary's hypotheses contain neither A5(ii) nor a rate product, so an appeal
to \textup{(i)} as stated would be an appeal to the \emph{proof} rather than to the statement;
\item[(ii)] if in addition $\hat\theta\xrightarrow{p}\theta_\dagger$ then
$\hat\Sigma\xrightarrow{p}\Sigma$ and $\hat V\xrightarrow{p}J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{A flag, not a side taken.} The influence function of \cref{thm:rootn} is $J^{-1}\psi_\star$, in which
$\varrho$ appears only through $\widetilde W$ at its true value, and no term correcting for the estimation of
$\varrho$ is present. That is a \emph{consequence} of \cref{prp:orthog}\textup{(iii)} under N1: the
$\varrho$-derivative of the moment vanishes \emph{exactly}, so there is nothing for a correction to remove.
\emph{The project's positioning section states the opposite}, that the sandwich carries an additional
correction for $\varrho$; the two statements cannot both be right, and the contradiction is recorded for the
writer at \S9 item~10 of the strategy memo rather than resolved here.
\end{lemma}

%  I.4  THE THEOREM
% ===========================================================================

\begin{theorem}[\texttt{thm:rootn}: asymptotic normality of the cross-fitted one-step estimator]\label{thm:rootn}
The one-step estimator is $\sqrt n$-consistent and asymptotically normal with the sandwich variance, under
mild ill-posedness and a propensity smooth enough to put the structural rate strictly inside $n^{-1/4}$.
% THE STATEMENT CARRIES CONDITIONS AND CONCLUSIONS AND NOTHING ELSE.  The
% hypothesis groups are tagged (T-1)--(T-5) and the additional hypotheses
% (R-a)--(R-e), on the model of prp:phirate's (P-a)--(P-g).  What each group
% does and does not carry is rem:rootngroups; how the conclusion is read is
% rem:rootnread.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A draft of this theorem tagged the groups (H1)--(H5).  H1 is the
% Hilbert-scale link, it is cited INSIDE group (T-5), and a group label reading
% "H1" next to an assumption tag reading "H1" is the collision this file has
% repaired four times elsewhere.
Suppose
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(T-1)] \emph{(sampling, model, identification)} A0; A1; A1b(i), A1b(iii), A1b(iv);
\item[(T-2)] \emph{(the representer and the weight)} A2; A$2'$(i.a), A$2'$(i.b), A$2'$(iii); N1 at
$L_\star$;
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A3 stood in this group through dispatch 12.  A3 is not in this
% group and no local rank condition on ell_star is either; rem:rootngroups(1).
\item[(T-3)] \emph{(index set, densities, propensity)} B1(i), (ii), (iv); C1(ii); C2$'$(i); A4(i),
A4(ii), A4(iii);
\item[(T-4)] \emph{(rates)} A5(i) and A5(ii) in the form \eqref{eq:deltalog}; A5(iii); and A5(vi) with
$s>\tfrac12$, read at each fold as in \cref{def:crossfit}(d);
% The group is NOT homogeneous in status: (T-5) delivers two of these clauses and
% no result in this file delivers A5(iii).  rem:rootngroups(2) records which is
% which, and why the (T-5) delivery does not make the listing redundant.
\item[(T-5)] \emph{(the $\varphi$-step)} the hypotheses of \cref{prp:phirate}, read at the anchor
$\theta_\circ$ of \cref{def:crossfit}(b) --- H1; A5(vi$'$); A8's basis and upper-end clauses;
$p_K\ge s-\tfrac12$; (P-a.1)--(P-a.3), (P-c)--(P-g); and \eqref{eq:muhalf}, $\mu>\tfrac56$ strictly ---
so that \eqref{eq:phirate} holds on each $\mathcal I_{-k}$;
\end{enumerate}
and suppose in addition
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(R-a)] \emph{(the weight is built as an anchored antiderivative, with a bounded derivative)} for each
$k$, $\hat L^{(-k)}=L^{\,\hat b^{(-k)}}_{\hat\ell^{(-k)}}$ in the sense of \cref{def:weight}(b), with
$\hat\ell^{(-k)}$ continuously differentiable in $u$ at every point and bounded,
\[
\max_{k\le\mathsf F}\Big\{\big\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}\big\|_\infty+\big\|\partial_u\hat\ell^{(-k)}\big\|_\infty\Big\}=O_P(1),
\qquad
\max_{k\le\mathsf F}E\big\|\hat b^{(-k)}(\Delta Z)\big\|^{4}=O_P(1),
\]
and $\max_{k\le\mathsf F}\|\hat L^{(-k)}-L_\star\|_{L^{2}(P)}=o_P(1)$;
% WHAT THIS CLAUSE DOES NOT REQUIRE -- sure boundedness of partial_u hat-ell --
% and what it adds to def:crossfit(c'.2)'s [0,+infty] typing: rem:rootngroups(3).
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  Dispatch 19 added a sure-boundedness conjunct on the ground that
% the two proof steps read finiteness straight off this hypothesis, and the same
% paragraph then recorded that "nothing was broken by the omission".  Both cannot
% be true of a minimal clause; the conjunct went and the O_P(1) display stayed, and
% the two proof sentences were re-grounded on the display rather than deleted.  A
% third site, thm:rootn Step 1, reads the clause only for the C^2 property of
% hat-L^{(-k)} and for the O_P rate, and is untouched either way.
\item[(R-b)] \emph{(fourth moments, and exactly two of them)} $E\|\Delta Z\|^{4}<\infty$ and
$E[\Delta U^{4}]<\infty$;
% Why a fourth moment of b_star is NOT needed: rem:rootngroups(4).
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft carried a third clause, E||b_star||^4 < infinity.
\item[(R-c)] \emph{(the $\varrho\times L$ cross term)} \textbf{either} \textup{(c.1)} $D_k=\hat L^{(-k)}-L_\star$
satisfies N1$'$ for every $k$, \textbf{or} \textup{(c.2)}
$\max_k\|D_k\|_{L^{2}(P)}=O_P(\epsilon^{L}_n)$ with $r_n\,\epsilon^{L}_n=o(n^{-1/2})$;
\item[(R-d)] \emph{(no hypothesis).} There is \textbf{no} hypothesis (R-d): the list runs (R-a), (R-b),
(R-c), (R-e), on the \textup{(P-b)} pattern above;
% The letter is reserved and not reused; rem:rootngroups(6).
\item[(R-e)] \emph{(the first-order bias)} \textbf{either} \textup{(e.1)} A5(iv) read at each fold, i.e.\ the
third display of \eqref{eq:foldrates} together with $\delta_n\epsilon_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})$, \textbf{or}
\textup{(e.2)} the hypotheses of \cref{lem:balance}\textup{(iii)} --- the sieve solve sets term
\textup{(II)} of \eqref{eq:balance3} to zero, A8 holds with a B-spline basis of degree exceeding
$s-\tfrac12$, A5(vi) holds and \eqref{eq:nuhat} holds --- together with
$\max_k\|\hat\ell^{(-k)}-\ell_\star\|_{L^{2}(P)}=o_P(1)$, \textbf{and} with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:re2window}
s\;>\;\frac{1}{2\,(1-2\alpha)} .
\end{equation}
% Why eq:re2window is stated on this branch and on no other, with the witness at
% which the branch would otherwise be empty: rem:rootngroups(5).
\end{enumerate}
Then, with $\hat\theta$ of \eqref{eq:onestep} and $J,\Sigma$ of \eqref{eq:JSig},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rootn}
\begin{split}
\sqrt n\,\big(\hat\theta-\theta_\dagger\big)
&\;=\;J^{-1}\,\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\psi_\star(O_i)\;+\;o_P(1)\\[2pt]
&\;\xrightarrow{\;d\;}\;\text{the centred Gaussian law on }\IR^{p}\text{ with covariance matrix }
J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime} ,
\end{split}
\end{equation}
and $\hat V\xrightarrow{p}J^{-1}\Sigma J^{-1\prime}$, so that for \textbf{every} $\vartheta\in\IR^{p}$ with
$\|\vartheta\|=1$,
\[
\sqrt n\,\vartheta'\big(\hat\theta-\theta_\dagger\big)\big/\big(\vartheta'\hat V\vartheta\big)^{1/2}
\;\xrightarrow{\;d\;}\;\text{the standard Gaussian law on }\IR ,
\]
the ratio being read on $\{\vartheta'\hat V\vartheta>0\}$, an event of probability tending to one.
% HOW THE CONCLUSION IS READ -- why the quantifier is "every" and not "every
% vartheta with vartheta' J^{-1} Sigma J^{-1'} vartheta > 0", why that is not a
% uniform lower bound, why the denominator can still vanish at finite n, what
% binds the letter vartheta, and why both limit laws are written out rather than
% given a symbol -- is rem:rootnread.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  Through dispatch 13 the quantifier read "every vartheta with
% vartheta' J^{-1} Sigma J^{-1'} vartheta > 0"; the change is a strengthening of
% the statement at no cost in hypotheses, and the entailment was found by probing
% this very display.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  Glossary C25.
% ARCHAEOLOGY (dispatch-23 change to how this theorem is PRINTED and to nothing it
% says).  Through dispatch 22 the two displays read N(0, J^{-1} Sigma J^{-1'}) and
% N(0,1) -- a law with two arguments on the letter lem:pfreeze's clause reserves.
% Step 5 of the proof already said "the limit law is written out and carries no
% symbol" while this statement printed the symbol twice.  The census behind glossary
% C84 named its own pattern as "N(", which does not match "N\big(", so the two
% displays here and the third at prp:medianpart were invisible to it: the proof was
% repaired and the three STATEMENTS were not.  Glossary C90 prints the per-file
% counts.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\emph{Notes on \cref{thm:rootn}.} What each hypothesis group does and does not carry is
\cref{rem:rootngroups}; how the conclusion is read is \cref{rem:rootnread}; what the theorem covers and the
six things it does not are \cref{rem:rootnscope}; the clause-by-clause usage audit is \cref{rem:rootnhyp};
the logarithm in \eqref{eq:phirate} is \cref{rem:rootnlog}.

\begin{corollary}[T2$'$: the rate floor, without \eqref{eq:frontier}]\label{cor:ratefloor}
The same decomposition delivers a rate whether or not the frontier holds; \emph{on the sieve branch, and
only there, every exponent in that rate is a function of the primitives}.
Suppose (T-1)--(T-3), (T-5), (R-a), (R-b) hold, together with A5(i), A5(vi) with $s>\tfrac12$,
$\delta_n\to0$, $\epsilon_n\to0$, $r_n\to0$, and (R-c.2), (R-e.1) with the two products left
\emph{unrestricted}. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ratefloor}
\big\|\hat\theta-\theta_\dagger\big\|
\;=\;O_P\Big(n^{-1/2}\;+\;\delta_n\epsilon_n\;+\;\delta_n^{2}\;+\;r_n\delta_n\;+\;r_n\epsilon^{L}_n\Big).
\end{equation}
Under (R-e.2) in place of (R-e.1) the term $\delta_n\epsilon_n$ is replaced by
$O_P(n^{-1/2}\delta_n)+O_P(\mathsf R\,L_x^{-s})$, and no rate for $\hat\ell$ enters
\eqref{eq:ratefloor} at all. Finally, \eqref{eq:rootn} is the special case of \eqref{eq:ratefloor} in
which every term after the first is $o(n^{-1/2})$.
% HOW MUCH OF eq:ratefloor IS IN PRIMITIVES, stated by branch because the answer
% differs by branch, and the sharper display available on the sieve branch:
% rem:ratefloorprim.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft of this corollary claimed the stronger of the two
% answers on the weaker branch.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  A round-10 draft listed a symbol "mu-prime", defined nowhere in
% this project and with no glossary row; it was deleted rather than defined.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\emph{Notes on \cref{cor:ratefloor}.} How much of \eqref{eq:ratefloor} is in primitives, and
which branch buys which answer, is \cref{rem:ratefloorprim}.

\begin{proposition}[L-10: the median over partitions]\label{prp:medianpart}
Averaging or taking medians over a fixed number of independent fold partitions changes neither the influence
function nor the limit.
Let $\mathsf P\ge1$ be fixed and not depending on $n$, let
$\hat\theta_1,\dots,\hat\theta_{\mathsf P}$ be the estimators \eqref{eq:onestep} computed on $\mathsf P$
partitions drawn independently of the data and indexed by $\mathsf p\in\{1,\dots,\mathsf P\}$
--- \emph{sans-serif, the lowercase of the count $\mathsf P$, and \textbf{not} $q$, which is bound to
$q=E[\widetilde W\partial_u\ell_\star\mid X_1,X_2]$} ---
and suppose the hypotheses of \cref{thm:rootn} hold
\textbf{at each partition}. \emph{The per-partition reading is part of the hypothesis and not a formality}:
the $\mathsf P$ partitions have $\mathsf P\mathsf F$ distinct fold complements, and (T-5), (R-a), (R-c),
(R-e) and \eqref{eq:foldrates} are conditions on the nuisances computed on a fold complement --- so what is
required is that they hold at all $\mathsf P\mathsf F$ of them, with the maxima in \eqref{eq:foldrates} and
(R-a) read over that index set. \emph{Since $\mathsf P$ and $\mathsf F$ are both fixed this is finitely many
statements and every order is preserved}; it is not a uniformity requirement, and it is a \emph{third} place
$\mathsf P$ fixed is doing work, beyond the two the proof names. Let
$\hat\theta^{\mathrm{md}}$ be their coordinatewise
median and $\hat\theta^{\mathrm{av}}:=\mathsf P^{-1}\sum_{\mathsf p}\hat\theta_{\mathsf p}$. Then
\[
\sqrt n\big(\hat\theta_{\mathsf p}-\hat\theta_{\mathsf p'}\big)=o_P(1)
\quad\text{for every }\mathsf p,\mathsf p',
\qquad
\sqrt n\big(\hat\theta^{\mathrm{md}}-\theta_\dagger\big)
=\sqrt n\big(\hat\theta^{\mathrm{av}}-\theta_\dagger\big)+o_P(1)
\;\xrightarrow{\;d\;}\;\text{the limit law of \eqref{eq:rootn}} .
\]
\emph{The limit is named by pointing at \eqref{eq:rootn} rather than by printing a symbol}, which is
\cref{thm:rootn}'s disposition carried to its third statement site and is also the more informative
form: what this proposition asserts \emph{is} that the median and the average have
\cref{thm:rootn}'s limit.
% ARCHAEOLOGY.  Glossary C90.
\emph{The argument is that all $\mathsf P$ estimators share one influence function, and it uses
$\mathsf P$ fixed three times}: once in the hypothesis, so that ``the hypotheses of \cref{thm:rootn} at each
partition'' is finitely many statements; once so that finitely many $o_P(1)$ terms may be collected; and once
so that the median is a continuous function of finitely many arguments. \emph{It says nothing about
$\mathsf P\to\infty$}, where the median would have to be handled as a functional of a random measure and the
hypothesis itself would become a uniformity requirement over a growing family of fold complements.
\end{proposition}
